author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare's commercial theatre served a city increasingly shaped by trade and credit. Venice gave him a setting where friendship, marriage and religious hostility could all become entangled with a debt.

hook.text: How generous are your principles when an enemy needs them?

paragraphs: A friend needs money. Antonio agrees to guarantee a loan, and Shylock proposes an extraordinary condition. Affection has entered a contract whose wording may matter more than anyone wishes.

The play asks what can be bought, promised, owed or forgiven. Its romantic plots make wealth a route towards marriage, while its central dispute exposes the violence inside religious exclusion. Characters who can speak beautifully about mercy do not necessarily offer it without conditions.

Shylock has been made one of literature's most troubling figures, and the play's antisemitism cannot be detached from the treatment he receives. His claims to dignity and his desire for retaliation make the audience's judgment difficult.
Read the speeches about justice and mercy with attention to who can afford each principle. Does generosity remain generous when it requires the recipient to become someone else?

orientation.text: The action moves between commercial Venice and Portia's household at Belmont. Read the anti-Jewish hostility as part of the play's world and its challenge to readers.
